subtitle: When the Karkota king carved a laughing capital from the Kashmiri plain

panels.shot: sweeping wide shot over misty Kashmir plain with faint ruins, ghosted vision of a radiant ancient city rising above
panels.action: Lalitaditya Muktapida stands on a sunlit rise above the Jhelum, cloak whipping in the wind, as an imagined Parihasapura glows behind him where only scattered stones lie today.

dialogue.text: In the age of the Karkotas, Lalitaditya built Parihasapura, the City of Laughter—palace, Vishnu shrines and a giant copper Buddha together—yet today almost nothing stands. How does a capital vanish, and a vision still endure?

i18n.hi: कार्कोटा युग में ललितादित्य ने बनाई परिहासपुरा — हँसी की नगरी: महल, विष्णु मंदिर और विशाल तांबे का बुद्ध एक साथ। आज वहाँ लगभग कुछ नहीं बचा। राजधानी कैसे गायब हुई, पर सपना कैसे ज़िंदा रहा?

panels.shot: epic aerial over the Kashmir valley, river Jhelum snaking through fields toward low hills
panels.action: Morning mist curls over the Jhelum as the river bends past green fields and a low rise near Paraspore; faint outlines of stone platforms suggest ancient foundations beneath.

dialogue.text: Northwest of Srinagar, above the Jhelum, the plain lies quiet. But Kalhana’s chronicle says this ground once held a planned royal city, laid out by a king who thought in stone and sunlight.

i18n.hi: श्रीनगर के उत्तर-पश्चिम, झेलम के ऊपर, मैदान चुप है। लेकिन कल्हण के इतिहास में यही ज़मीन एक बसाई हुई राजनगरी है, पत्थर और धूप में सोचने वाले राजा की बनाई हुई।

panels.shot: medium shot, low-angle, Lalitaditya on a temporary wooden viewing platform overlooking the open plain
panels.action: Lalitaditya stands with surveying staff in hand, pointing toward the horizon as attendants and builders listen, the flat expanse below marked with wooden stakes and chalked lines.

dialogue.text: Around the 740s, Lalitaditya Muktapida turned from campaigns to creation. Here, near modern Paraspore, he chose a bare rise for a new royal seat: Parihasapura, City of Laughter.

i18n.hi: ७४० के आसपास ललितादित्य मुक्तपीड ने युद्ध से रचना की ओर रुख किया। आज के परसपुर के पास, उसने सूनी ऊँचाई चुनी नई राज-सीट के लिए: परिहासपुरा, हँसी की नगरी।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Lalitaditya’s thoughtful face as he studies a palm-leaf plan
panels.action: Seated under a canopy, Lalitaditya leans over palm-leaf sketches showing aligned rectangles and courtyards, a stylus poised, a court architect kneeling beside him indicating axes with a drawn thread.

dialogue.text: Kalhana lists not one shrine but a whole complex: palace, Vishnu temples, a chaitya and a towering Buddha. This was urban planning, not just piety—a city to declare what Kashmir had become.

i18n.hi: कल्हण एक मंदिर नहीं, पूरा समूह गिनते हैं: महल, विष्णु के मंदिर, चैत्य और विशाल बुद्ध। यह सिर्फ भक्ति नहीं, शहर की योजना थी — कश्मीर क्या बन चुका है, यह दिखाने वाली नगरी।

panels.shot: wide construction shot, bird’s-eye over coordinated building sites
panels.action: The plain is alive with activity: foundation trenches cut in grids, stone blocks hauled by teams, timber scaffolds rising around multiple future halls while Lalitaditya rides through the works inspecting.

dialogue.text: At Parihasapura, royal and sacred buildings rose together. The palace and the temples shared courtyards and sight-lines, binding king, gods and Buddha into one planned landscape.

i18n.hi: परिहासपुरा में राजमहल और देवालय साथ-साथ उठे। महल और मंदिरों के आँगन और नज़रें जुड़ी थीं, राजा, देवों और बुद्ध को एक ही सजाई हुई धरती में बाँधते हुए।

panels.shot: low-angle shot along a colonnade of the emerging palace
panels.action: Rows of newly set stone pillars stretch toward a central hall, craftsmen chiseling capitals while Lalitaditya walks between them, hand brushing the cool stone, measuring height against the sky.

dialogue.text: Kalhana calls the royal residence at Parihasapura a palace that invited laughter—parihasa—by its delight. The name itself tied joy to power, as if the capital should smile in stone.

i18n.hi: कल्हण परिहासपुरा के राजमहल को ऐसा भवन कहते हैं जो आनंद से परिहास — हँसी — बुलाए। नाम ही सत्ता को खुशियों से जोड़ता है, जैसे राजधानी खुद पत्थर में मुस्कुराए।

panels.shot: wide shot of temple plinths being laid out with geometric precision
panels.action: Builders set massive bases for shrines in exact relation: one platform larger, flanked by two slightly smaller ones, a central axis running through toward the palace court where Lalitaditya watches intently.

dialogue.text: To one side he ordered grand Vishnu temples; to another, a Buddhist chaitya. Their positions were no accident. The city’s plan itself showed a ruler who placed different paths side by side.

i18n.hi: एक ओर उसने विराट विष्णु मंदिर खड़े करवाए; दूसरी ओर बौद्ध चैत्य। उनकी जगहें सोची-समझी थीं। शहर की रचना ही दिखाती है कि शासक ने अलग राहों को साथ रखा।

panels.shot: dramatic low-angle on framework of enormous Buddha statue under construction
panels.action: A towering wooden armature dwarfs the workers below; sheets of hammered copper are being fixed in place, ladders clinging to its sides, as Lalitaditya gazes up at the emerging figure in awe.

dialogue.text: Most striking, Kalhana describes a colossal Buddha image, sheathed in shining copper. Its exact height is lost in royal exaggeration, but its scale and metallic gleam marked a new ambition.

i18n.hi: सबसे चौंकाने वाली बात, कल्हण एक महाबुद्ध प्रतिमा का वर्णन करते हैं, चमकते तांबे में ढकी हुई। ऊँचाई राजा की अतिशयोक्ति में खो गई, पर उसका पैमाना और तेज़ चमक नई महत्वाकांक्षा दिखाते हैं।

panels.shot: close-up on copper plates and gilding tools laid out on mats
panels.action: Artisans squat around copper panels, carving fine lines, while others burnish gold leaf onto test strips; Lalitaditya’s fingers hover above the metal, catching reflected light from the afternoon sun.

dialogue.text: Kalhana’s verses revel in gold, silver and copper. The exact quantities are courtly flourish, yet they point to real monumental wealth—metal used not just as ornament but as architectural skin.

i18n.hi: कल्हण के श्लोक सोने, चाँदी और तांबे में डूबे हैं। आँकड़े दरबारी सजावट हैं, पर इशारा असली विराट संपदा की ओर है — धातु जो सिर्फ सजावट नहीं, इमारत की खाल बन गई।

panels.shot: wide ceremonial shot of the completed core complex
panels.action: Under clear skies, the palace, Vishnu shrines and the gleaming Buddha stand complete around a vast paved court filled with courtiers and monks as Lalitaditya climbs a central stair, banners streaming.

dialogue.text: When the core was ready, the city looked like a stone mandala: king’s court at the center, Vaishnava shrines and Buddhist sanctuaries radiating out. Parihasapura announced a Karkota world in balance.

i18n.hi: जब केंद्र तैयार हुआ, शहर पत्थर का मंडल जैसा दिखा: बीच में राजदरबार, चारों ओर फैलती वैष्णव और बौद्ध देवस्थली। परिहासपुरा ने संतुलित कार्कोटा संसार की घोषणा की।

panels.speaker: lalitaditya_muktapida
panels.shot: medium shot on a balcony overlooking the complex at dusk
panels.action: Lalitaditya stands alone at his palace balcony at twilight, watching lamps flicker to life in the temple courtyards and around the looming copper Buddha, his face calm but intent.

dialogue.text: From his balcony the king saw not just buildings, but a message: that Kashmir’s ruler could sit amid many devotions, that laughter, light and learning belonged inside the frame of royal power.

i18n.hi: अपनी बालकनी से राजा ने सिर्फ इमारतें नहीं, संदेश देखा: कि कश्मीर का शासक अनेक उपासनाओं के बीच बैठ सकता है, और हँसी, रोशनी और विद्या राजसत्ता की चौखट के भीतर हैं।

panels.shot: slow push-in on mixed gathering in the main court
panels.action: In the central court, Brahmins, Buddhists, officials and traders mingle, some gesturing toward the various shrines while Lalitaditya listens to a report from a councilor at his throne-platform.

dialogue.text: Parihasapura functioned as more than a showpiece. Kalhana’s careful temple list hints at ongoing ritual and patronage, making the city a lived center of Karkota administration and religion.

i18n.hi: परिहासपुरा सिर्फ दिखावे की नगरी नहीं थी। कल्हण की सावधानी से गिनाई मंदिर सूची चलती पूजा और संरक्षण की ओर इशारा करती है, शहर को कार्कोटा शासन और धर्म का जीता-जागता केंद्र बनाती है।

panels.shot: contrast panel, modern-era wide shot of scattered stone bases at Paraspore
panels.action: Centuries later, under a gray sky, low stone platforms and broken pillars lie in farm fields near Paraspore; a dirt road cuts through, with quarried blocks reused in its edging.

dialogue.text: By Stein’s visit in 1892, much had already gone. Stones from Parihasapura’s platforms edged new roads; pillars lay fallen in fields. The planned city survived only as ruins and a memory in verse.

i18n.hi: १८९२ में स्टाइन के आने तक बहुत कुछ जा चुका था। परिहासपुरा के चबूतरे की पत्थर नई सड़कों के किनारे लग गए; स्तंभ खेतों में गिर पड़े। बसाई हुई नगरी अब सिर्फ खंडहर और श्लोकों की याद बनकर बची।

panels.shot: close-up on an archaeologist’s hand tracing a carved stone at the site
panels.action: A modern researcher kneels beside a weathered block, fingertips tracing faint mouldings while a notebook lies open beside a copy of Kalhana’s Rajatarangini and Stein’s site plan.

dialogue.text: Stein matched Kalhana’s description to Paraspore’s ruins, sketching plans where stratigraphy is still thin. Without full excavation, scholars like Goetz read the stones and texts together for clues.

i18n.hi: स्टाइन ने कल्हण के वर्णन को परसपुर के खंडहरों से मिलाया, जहाँ परतें अभी पतली हैं वहाँ नक्शे खींचे। पूरी खुदाई के बिना, गोएट्ज जैसे विद्वान पत्थरों और ग्रंथों को जोड़कर संकेत खोजते हैं।

panels.shot: illustrative montage of art influences radiating outward on a map
panels.action: An abstract map glows, Kashmir at the center, stylized temple and Buddha silhouettes spreading in faint lines toward neighboring regions, hinting at artistic dialogues rather than specific copies.

dialogue.text: Art historians see in Parihasapura’s complex signs of wider influence—a Kashmiri way of arranging palace and shrines that may have echoed in Himalayan and north Indian building in later centuries.

i18n.hi: कला इतिहासकार परिहासपुरा के समूह में दूर तक फैले असर के संकेत देखते हैं — महल और देवालयों को सजाने का कश्मीरी अंदाज़, जिसकी गूँज हिमालय और उत्तर भारत की बाद की इमारतों में दिख सकती है।

panels.shot: evocative fade between Lalitaditya’s ancient silhouette and the present-day ruins
panels.action: Lalitaditya’s figure stands ghost-like over the plain, gradually dissolving into the present view of broken platforms and fields, the Jhelum winding beyond as clouds drift overhead.

dialogue.text: Parihasapura no longer laughs in stone. Yet through Kalhana’s careful verses and the scattered remains, Lalitaditya’s experiment in shaping a capital as a statement of identity still speaks to us.

i18n.hi: परिहासपुरा अब पत्थर में नहीं हँसती। पर कल्हण की बारीक पंक्तियों और छिटके अवशेषों के बीच, राजधानी को पहचान का बयान बनाकर गढ़ने का ललितादित्य का प्रयोग आज भी हमसे बात करता है।

title_i18n.en: Lalitaditya Builds the City That Laughed
title_i18n.hi: ललितादित्य ने बनाई हँसती हुई नगरी

subtitle_i18n.en: When the Karkota king carved a laughing capital from the Kashmiri plain
subtitle_i18n.hi: जब कार्कोटा राजा ने कश्मीर के मैदानी ज़मीन से हँसती राजधानी تراशी
